source.title: LORENZA: Enhancing Generalization in Low-Rank Gradient LLM Training via Efficient Zeroth-Order Adaptive SAM
source.authors: Yehonathan Refael; Iftach Arbel; Ofir Lindenbaum; Tom Tirer

record.tranche_reason: The study uses sharpness-aware minimization as a way to seek flatter minima and improve generalization, then evaluates its own optimization method. It does not test any listed claim version directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports benchmark results for LORENZA and comparison methods, but does not measure random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected architecture, adaptive optimizers versus SGD, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness versus the train–test gap, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study uses the premise that flatter minima improve generalization to design LORENZA and evaluates its benchmark performance. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with train–test gaps, or its ranking against other measures (V7). Its other experiments do not implement the comparisons or interventions named in V1–V6 or V8. Adam-based method comparisons and convergence proofs using SGD do not test adaptive optimizers against SGD (V4).
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' conclusion: LORENZA combines zeroth-order adaptive SAM with low-rank updates to improve accuracy and memory/computational efficiency in LLM training and fine-tuning. The authors claim improved generalization and provide stationary-point convergence guarantees. Their benchmark results do not independently establish the magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship, and superiority is not uniform across all tasks or full-rank comparisons.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a new low-rank adaptive SAM optimizer using zeroth-order ascent estimation; evaluations concern LLM pre-training and fine-tuning rather than the claim versions’ interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported GLUE metrics vary by task and rank; pre-training validation perplexity varies by token count. The study does not report these as tests of any listed version.

fits_no_version.finding: LORENZA reports GLUE scores, C4 validation perplexities, and GSM8K accuracies relative to other training methods. These evaluate the proposed optimizer without measuring any listed claim's specified comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Combining zeroth-order SAM perturbations with low-rank adaptive updates can improve held-out LLM performance relative to other memory-efficient methods in the tested settings.

record.problems: The text reports benchmark scores without uncertainty estimates. It does not report training error alongside held-out metrics, so train–test gaps cannot be determined. Several evaluation details are not stated in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 comparator methods and Table 3 pre-training method comparisons were left out because they report comparisons among methods rather than outcomes attributable to a listed claim version. The baseline model and other methods in Tables 5–6 were also omitted for the same reason.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and the corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Network-width sweeps beyond zero training error and their test-error trends.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and word-level language-model comparisons.
Batch-size comparisons at fixed epoch budgets and changes to recipes or training duration.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance correlated with train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equal-sized random removals and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded numerical scores match the supplied tables. Rows R1–R21 describe the study's own method performance and should not serve as phenomenon-result rows. Missing train–test gaps specifically preclude V7 analysis; other versions are untested because their required interventions or comparisons are absent. Figure 1 is an attributed illustration, not an original sharpness experiment. No additional version-bearing results require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited tuning, broader tuning, weight decay, switching optimizers, and language-model comparisons.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects and removing dropout and weight decay together.
Magnitude-aware sharpness compared with train–test gaps and other generalization measures.
Removing high-influence memorized examples and measuring test-accuracy change.
